steps.why: The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.

steps.rule: The see-through layer behind a modal.
steps.pick: black.light.scrim: a see-through layer that dims the page behind a modal, so the dialog is the one thing to act on.
steps.darkPick: black.dark.scrim: a see-through layer that dims the page behind a modal, so the dialog is the one thing to act on.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.2:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So readers see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by a 12px offset and a 32px blur in a 16% warm brown. So a menu lifts off warm paper without a hard edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are soft (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light shadow's shape for menus and dialogs in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 12px offset and 32px blur, at 50% black instead of 16% brown. So a menu still lifts off the dark page, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and dark ships for night reading (theming.values).

steps.pick: radius.12: We use a 12px corner for article cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a warm tone by brand convention. A larger radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 8px controls inside it. So a card reads as one calm object on the page, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is warm (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
steps.pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line, 1.35:1 on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So readers see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line, 1.46:1 on surface.raised (#4A4339, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So readers see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
steps.pick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.12:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0: We use one step darker than content for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.1:1 on surface.default. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.pick: radius.8: We use the 8px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list item or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So fields and rows read as one family, because the control corner is rounded, not a pill (shape.values), and the brand is warm (brand.q1).
